# Genuine AMC v1.1.1 migration fixtures

These fixtures were generated on 2026-10-16 from the unchanged `v1.1.1` source at `ff53902225ff276c55558d5ca17a8fc60b780655`. The configured official remote and local annotated tag matched object `833417ce78fafb0daa0af26f06323b045fe331b9`; this is an observed ref match, not tag-signature authentication. The historical `npm ci` and `npm run build` passed with the original package and lock unchanged, using Node 22.23.3 and a release-local native module.

`originals.tar.gz` stores eight exact original files losslessly: diagnostic and assurance reports, signed trust-certificate JSON, passport and bundle containers, a domain report, a derived ledger observation, and a naturally closed SQLite snapshot containing only inline imported and dogfood events, captured before diagnostic and assurance runs. `provenance.json` records every original byte count and SHA256, its generating command or exported API, the generator/runtime/source pins, actual process results and retained private evidence locations. `generation.log` summarizes those actual commands. Tests must verify every decoded original against those hashes before use. The directory's stored bytes, including this note and metadata, remain below 1,000,000; the decoded originals are larger. No original content, signature or embedded public verification key was edited to meet the size limit. Raw `.amc/keys`, vaults and private keys are excluded.

The assurance report genuinely ran the old canned-response implementation. The operator import used explicitly synthetic input and the old operator-selected OBSERVED tier; dogfood output remains synthetic. The domain report came from the old exported builder, with no paid CLI entitlement claim. The ledger-observation JSON is derived from actual old public getters at that same pre-assessment snapshot, not an independently emitted historical report. All nine captured events have inline payloads and no blob dependency. The full later workspace ledger remains retained privately; no rows were removed from it. `ledgerSnapshot.sourceAtClosure` is a historical pin at capture time, not a claim that the later workspace database stayed unchanged.

The diagnostic's actual mean level is L0. The unchanged default certificate gate refused issuance, so no diagnostic `.amccert` or genuine L3 case is claimed. Unversioned trust-certificate JSON and passport formats remain distinguishability/reader bounds. A separate unchanged full dogfood run later emitted a genuine default-policy certificate at mean level 3.923; that complete 1,996,064-byte certificate remains private because it does not fit this corpus cap. It does not satisfy the exact-L3 case. The core generator exits 1 to retain its actual gaps. Fixture generation, signature integrity, legacy claim labels and complete P1-35 acceptance are separate evidence.

## Why a binary archive, and its size

`originals.tar.gz` is 709,335 bytes, sha256 `bd08c2bad43869ffce02571a6db9411305df77db7b5a77576ad8065c4655782c`; `provenance.json` pins the same bytes and digest under `storage.archive`, and the tests refuse the corpus if either differs. It decodes to the eight originals, 4,104,713 bytes in total, each checked against its own `candidates[].source` pin before any test reads it. It stays one compressed archive because the classifier and the integrity readers need the originals byte for byte: signed bundle and certificate bytes, a SQLite snapshot and a 3.3 MB diagnostic report cannot be trimmed or re-serialized without becoming a different artifact, and stored uncompressed they would take about 4.1 MB instead of 0.7 MB. The absolute `/private/tmp/...` paths in `provenance.json` record where generation ran; they are not needed to verify the archive. To regenerate it, run `scripts/make-legacy-fixtures.mjs` with `--legacy-source` set to a built `v1.1.1` checkout; `generation.log` summarizes the commands it ran.
